subject: Concealing cables and equipment
hook: Trailing cables, an extension lead behind the sofa, boxes on the floor. Here is how that corner gets sorted.
ig:
Trailing cables, an extension lead behind the sofa, boxes on the floor. Here is how that corner gets sorted.

This is a typical journey from a cluttered TV wall to a media wall where nothing shows:

1. The starting point: a wall-mounted TV with cables dropping to a pile of equipment.
2. Count the kit, so every device gets its own shelf and power.
3. Get sockets moved by an electrician before the furniture is fitted.
4. Design the route: a void behind the back panel, cable holes where needed, and a lift-out access panel.
5. Build it in the workshop, square and quality-checked.
6. Fit it, feed the cables through, then mount the TV.

The order matters. Most messy media walls happen when step three gets skipped and the sockets end up in the wrong place.

Want to see real finished work? Our showcase is linked in bio.
fb:
Most of us have a corner like this somewhere: the TV on the wall, a tangle of cables down to the floor, and an extension lead hiding behind the sofa.

Here is the typical route to sorting it properly. Count the equipment, get the sockets moved to where they are needed, design a cable route into the unit, build it, then fit it with everything fed through before the TV goes back up.

The step people skip is the sockets. Get those right and the rest falls into place. See finished work from our Hanley workshop here:
